texts.preamble: Khuma Ram And Anr vs State (2025:Rj-Jd:5801) on 29 January, 2025 Author: Kuldeep Mathur Bench: Kuldeep Mathur [2025:Rj-Jd:5801] High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan At Jodhpur S.B. Criminal Revision Petition No. 465/2006 1. Khuma Ram S/o Kana Ji, R/o Malgaon, Tehsil Reodar, District Sirohi 2. M/s Ramesh Kumar Khumaji Malgaon ----Petitioner Versus The State of Rajasthan ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. S.K. Verma For Respondent(s) : Mr. Shrawan Singh Rathore, Pp Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Kuldeep Mathur Order 29/01/2025
texts.facts: As per prosecution, on 09.03.1993 the samples of chilli powder were taken from the petitioner No.1 who is proprietor of petitioner No.2 - firm. The samples were sent for examination to the Public Analyst, Jodhpur after duly following the procedure provided under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. On the basis of the report of the Public Analyst, the petitioner was prosecuted for the offence under section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. During the course of trial, the prosecution examined as many as 5 witnesses and 20 documents were exhibited.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner does not have any criminal antecedents. He further submitted that the incident in the present case occurred in the year 1993. There is no positive evidence available on record regarding the adding of starch and artificial colour in the red chilli powder by the petitioner and in the absence thereof, only on the basis of the report of Public Analyst, it cannot be said that the petitioner had committed the alleged crime or the red chilli powder was adulterated. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the sentence awarded to the petitioner has alreadyu been suspended by this Court vide order dated 20.06.2006. Learned counsel for the petitioner in the alternative submitted that since the occurrence relates to year 1993 and the petitioner has already served some part of the sentence awarded to him, therefore, the substantive sentence awarded to the petitioner may be reduced to the period already undergone by him. Reliance was placed on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Puttaswamy v State of Karnataka: 2009 (1) WLC (SC) (Cri.) 623 and a judgment of Coordinate [2025:RJ-JD:5801] (3 of 4) [CRLR-465/2006] Bench of this Court in the case of Kamla Prasad v. State of Rajasthan: 2014 CriLJ 2582. Per Contra learned Public Prosecutor submitted that the learned courts below have rightly awarded the sentence against the petitioner.

Learned counsel for the petitioner in the alternative submitted that since the occurrence relates to year 1993 and the petitioner has already served some part of the sentence awarded to him, therefore, the substantive sentence awarded to the petitioner may be reduced to the period already undergone by him.

State of Rajasthan: 2014 CriLJ 2582. Per Contra learned Public Prosecutor submitted that the learned courts below have rightly awarded the sentence against the petitioner.
